name: organisation
title: Organisation
description: Who this organisation is and what it does, in its own words and its own vocabulary.

files.organisation.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE ORGANISATION (docs/unoverse/data/objects/elements/organisation.md): the one that owns this
# spatial. Never a row: it is the scope on every row (`org`) and the grounding every run wakes
# with, so it declares no embed, no search, no uniqueBy, and does not extend the base.
type: object
name: organisation
element: organisation
# THE GLYPH its rows are drawn with (README 4a): a lucide icon name.
icon: building-2

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it: what this is and when an Agent reaches for it.
title: Organisation
description: >-
  Who this organisation is and what it does, in its own words and its own vocabulary.
whenToUse: >-
  Ground any extraction, any agent or any piece of writing in who the organisation is and
  how it speaks. Read whole at wake, never searched for. The plain facts of the business and
  its vocabulary: what it is, and the words it uses for its products, its customers and
  itself.
category: Identity
version: 1.0.0

props: { $include: props }
files.props.yaml:
# THE ORGANISATION DOCUMENT'S FIELDS. Its `what` and `vocabulary` are the grounding.
name:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    The org's name as it trades, exactly as its website writes it in its own header or
    footer. Never a legal suffix unless the site uses one.
  maxLength: 80
what:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    One paragraph, 60 to 120 words, in the third person: what the business is, what it
    does, whom it serves, where. Taken from the site's own about, home and footer copy.
    This paragraph grounds every extraction, so it must name the business's actual lines
    of work, not adjectives. Never a slogan, never an industry generality.
  maxLength: 900
units:
  type: array
  input: true
  description: >-
    The organisation map: every unit the organisation names in its own publications, the
    ones that face customers (divisions, lines of business, regions) and the ones that run
    the organisation (operations, technology, people and HR, finance, risk, legal,
    marketing, and the rest). Sources: the about and careers pages, the annual report's
    organisation or leadership section, a published org chart. One entry per unit with its
    name as the organisation writes it and one sentence on what it does or serves, nested
    in `units` where the organisation nests them. Empty when the sources name none; never
    invented.
  maxItems: 40
  items:
    name:
      type: string
      description: >-
        The name as the organisation writes it.
      maxLength: 80
    what:
      type: string
      description: >-
        One sentence, in the organisation's words.
      maxLength: 240
    units:
      type: array
      description: >-
        The nested units, in the same shape, where the organisation nests them.
vocabulary:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    The words the business uses, as one paragraph separated by semicolons: its product and
    service names as it spells them, its programme and membership names, the terms it uses
    for its customers, and anything it capitalises. Every name is copied from the site,
    never paraphrased. This is the domain prompt every extraction reads, so completeness
    beats elegance.
  maxLength: 2000
